title: A Reponse to the Sheldon Goldstein Objection to a Series of Covariant Relativistic Bohmian Models
abstract: In this work we try to answer a very important objection to the Covariant Bohmian Models type Nikolić and Hernández-Zapata that was formulated by the american physicist Sheldon Goldstein (private communication, 2010) about the imposibility to interpret the configuration space-time density found by the authors of these models like a probability density. The problem is that it is very dificult to show that the N space-time configuration density has a finite integral. That is very important in order to normalize the density to produce a PDF (probability density function). All the steps in the demonstrations seemed complete but this objection must be resolved imperatively before to continue using this kind of models with full confidence. Since the aim of Bohmian Mechanics (also known as the De Broglie-Bohm Mechanics) is to provide a precise and objective formulation of Quantum Mechanics free from vagueness and obscurity (Bell point of view at least), addressing this issue is crucial. In this article, we set out to tackle this by employing a specific type of function that we call an "Arrangement Function".
summary: This paper tackles a fundamental mathematical objection to covariant Bohmian models concerning the normalization of their space-time density. The authors introduce an 'Arrangement Function' as a novel tool to mathematically regularize the theory, allowing for a consistent, Lorentz-covariant description of relativistic quantum dynamics. This resolves a major hurdle in applying Bohmian mechanics to modern field theories.
main_problem: The primary goal is resolving Sheldon Goldstein's objection regarding the non-integrability of the configuration space-time density in Covariant Bohmian Models, which prevents its normalization to a probability density function.
main_result: The authors propose using a novel 'Arrangement Function' ($\mathcal{A}$) to construct an integrable framework that allows for Lorentz-covariant descriptions while maintaining mathematical consistency for defining a proper PDF.
method: They employ the Arrangement Function to modify continuity equations and guide equations, restricting quantum interactions to be strictly spacelike separations within the formalism.
model_or_system: The work extends Bohmian Mechanics to relativistic quantum field theories (Klein-Gordon and Dirac Equations) in a covariant manner, treating particle paths through space-time density rather than simple foliations.
key_observables: Space-Time Density ($ho$), the integral convergence $ ar{A}$ (which must be finite), and the resulting Bohmian Guide Equations for particle trajectories.
important_parameters: Planck's constant ($\hbar$), speed of light ($c$), and the structure of the Arrangement Function itself, which dictates interaction locality.
main_assumptions: The necessity of introducing the 'Arrangement Function' to enforce mathematical integrability; assuming quantum interactions are strictly spacelike while classical ones are timelike.
paper_structure: The paper systematically addresses the Klein-Gordon model, introduces the Arrangement Function for spacelike restriction, tackles Goldstein's objection by ensuring finite integral convergence ($ ar{A}$), and concludes with an analysis of the Dirac Equation case.
why_interesting: While not directly focused on AMO systems like cold atoms or cavity QED, the rigorous development of a consistent quantum mechanical framework (Bohmian Mechanics) for relativistic particles is foundational theoretical work that impacts how one models non-local dynamics in complex quantum systems.
